title: Psychological Operations (PSYOP) Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC I
raw_text:
8. MOS 0520, Psychological Operations (PSYOP) Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt)
FMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. PSYOP Officers plan and execute functions pertaining to
military information support operations (MISO). Influence Officer is defined
as the trained personnel who primarily plan and conduct MISO, but can also,
in certain contexts, conduct civil authorities’ information support (CAIS)
and military deception (MILDEC). MISO are planned operations to convey
selected information and indicators to foreign audiences to influence their
emotions, motives, objective reasoning, and, ultimately, the behavior of
foreign governments, organizations, groups, and individuals in a manner
favorable to the originator’s objectives. Influence Officers capabilities
are critical to the success of the marine air ground task force (MAGTF)
mission, as they enable commanders to shape the information and security
environment in their areas of responsibility (AOR). This MOS will be
assigned to unrestricted officers as a non-PMOS only by the CMC (MM). This
MOS will be transitioning completely to the 1707 PMOS.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     secret security clearance.




                                            1-35                        Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) Must be currently in or have orders to fill a PSYOP Officer
billet.

        (3) Captains or below of any MOS; and majors or above will require
concurrence from the MOS specialist.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete an approved Military Psychological Operations Officer’s
Course (A05M301), Ft Liberty, NC.

        (2) Complete the MAGTF Operations in the Information Environment
Practitioner Course (MOPC) (M02F2GD), Quantico, VA.

        (3) Any of these requirements may be waived by the Deputy Commandant
for Information based on unique work or educational experience.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Assists in the development of USMC doctrine on MISO consistent
with USMC policy.

        (2) Provides subject matter expertise to the development of USMC
policy on MISO consistent with DoD policy.

        (3) Analyses target audiences, evaluates effects of MISO; and knows
the techniques and methodology of MISO.

        (4) Develops MISO plans and advises the commander on the conduct of
MISO for all operations, contingencies and exercises.

        (5) Coordinates with other combined and joint services and other
government agency PSYOP/MISO organizations to meet mission requirements.

        (6) Conducts MISO as may be required or directed by the commander
during all phases of operations. This includes directly supporting forward
deployed maneuver elements as a member a MISO detachment as well as
supporting staff planning at the headquarters/command element level.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders/Managers, All Other
55-1019.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Civil-Military Operations Planner, 1708.

            (2) Advanced Information Operations (IO) Planner, 1709.

            (3) Civil Affairs Officer, 1730.

            (4) Basic Information Planner, 1781.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
